statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Spanish language using Latin alphabet; no transliteration required for foreign names but must comply with Spanish orthography
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Protected company names, descriptive terms, words infringing trademarks, religious or political connotations, names similar to public entities
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of name reservation, administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) may be filed before the competent authority within one month; further judicial appeal available

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Spanish Capital Companies Act); applicable Articles 1-23 (incorporation), 28-31 (registered office), 58-66 (corporate domicile), 89-99 (minimum share capital for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada), 102-110 (participations), 209-213 (administrators), and 226-227 (first board resolutions); supplementary application of Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Mercantile Registry Regulations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name certification) and Registro Mercantil Provincial de Madrid (constitutive inscription and corporate registration); registry oversight by the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public deed of incorporation) executed before a Spanish notary, followed by mandatory inscription in the Registro Mercantil and publication in the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada requires minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at incorporation; capital is divided into participaciones not negotiable securities. The full amount must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (cuenta restringida) at a Spanish credit institution before deed execution; the bank issues a deposit certificate, the funds remain blocked until registry inscription, and the certificate is cancelled post-registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: That part of the subscribed capital of EUR 3,000 being fully subscribed and paid into the blocked account, the issuance of participations to each founding member is hereby approved. The registered office is fixed at Calle de Serrano 10, 28001 Madrid, within the jurisdiction of the Madrid Mercantile Registry, and adoption of this corporate seat is ratified. Don/Doña [Name] is appointed Sole Administrator with the powers granted by Article 62 of the Capital Companies Act, and Don/Doña [Name] is appointed Non-Member Secretary; both accept their offices. The Administrator is authorized to execute all filings before the Mercantile Registry, the State Tax Agency, the Official Gazette (BORME) and all other authorities to perfect incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Calle Príncipe de Vergara 94, Madrid, or telematically through the CIRCE Entrepreneur Service Portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for a Negative Name Certification (certificación negativa de denominación social) listing up to three alternative corporate names in order of preference. The registry verifies that no identical or confusingly similar denomination is registered and issues the certificate, which remains valid for three months. The certificate must be attached to the deed of incorporation and to the registry filing.
required_dossiers: Standard application form for negative name certification
Passports or NIE cards of all founding shareholders
Power of attorney if a legal representative acts on behalf of incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is withheld because of a name conflict, within five business days file an amended application reordering or replacing the proposed names; the Registro Mercantil Central permits resubmission without additional penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of Minimum Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution selected by the founding shareholders, supervised by the Bank of Spain.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the name of the company in formation (denominación social en constitución) and deposit the full minimum capital of EUR 3,000. The bank issues a deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) evidencing the blocked funds; the certificate is presented to the notary at deed execution and later to the Mercantile Registry. The funds remain blocked until registration is perfected.
required_dossiers: Passports or NIE cards of incorporators
Negative name certificate issued by the Registro Mercantil Central
Draft bylaws or constitution project
Bank KYC/AML forms and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence queries, provide audited source-of-funds documentation and a sworn beneficial-ownership declaration within ten business days; alternatively select another credit institution and re-deposit the capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público (Civil Law Notary) in the province of the registered office, Madrid.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the escritura de constitución before the notary, integrating the name certificate, bank deposit certificate, identity details of the incorporators, and the estatutos (bylaws) including the corporate object covering private-equity syndicated leveraged buyouts under ISIC 6499. The notary verifies the legal capacity of the incorporators and the mandatory content under Articles 22 and 23 of the Capital Companies Act, then authenticates the deed protocol.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate in force
Bank deposit certificate proving EUR 3,000 paid in
Bylaws draft approved by all founding shareholders
Passports or NIE cards of all founding members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary observes defects in the corporate object clause or bylaws, amend the draft accordingly and re-execute the deed; a second signature within the same proceeding generally carries no additional professional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Provisional Tax Identification Code (NIF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Delegación Provincial de Madrid, via the electronic headquarters.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of deed execution, file Model 036 (census declaration) attaching a first copy of the deed of incorporation to obtain the provisional corporate NIF. The provisional NIF remains valid six months pending registry inscription and must be replaced with the definitive NIF within two months after registration.
required_dossiers: Copy of the notarized deed of incorporation
Model 036 tax census registration form
Identity documents of the appointed administrator(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT issues a query on the application, submit the original notarial protocol or first copy of the deed, rectify discrepancies on Model 036, and resubmit electronically within the granted term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Mercantile Registry and Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the first notarial copy (primera copia) of the public deed to the Madrid Mercantile Registry within one month of notarization for constitutive inscription. The registry verifies legality, registers the company, and the registration is published in the BORME. If inscription is sought after one month, a supplementary deed confirming no change in constitutional statements is required.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy of the deed of incorporation
Negative name certificate
Bank deposit certificate
Model 600 proving settlement of Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty (ITP/AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a calificación suspension or defect note, execute a supplementary deed (escritura complementaria) curing the defect, or appeal the qualification before the Juzgado de lo Mercantil within the statutory two-month term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Officer Acceptance and Post-Registration Closing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal corporate body, with filings before the Registro Mercantil Provincial de Madrid, AEAT, and SEPBLAC as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution, subscribing share participations, fixing the registered office, and appointing officers. Record the resolution in the corporate minute book, file officer acceptance documents, update the definitive NIF through Model 036, register beneficial ownership in the Registro de Titularidades Reales, and, because the vehicle is a private-equity SPV, notify SEPBLAC of the company's status for AML surveillance.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution
Officers' acceptance letters
Updated Model 036 with definitive NIF
Definitive NIF certificate issued by AEAT
BORME publication excerpt
Beneficial ownership registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or AEAT rejects any post-formation filing, correct the minute book or census data as required and refile; a licensed corporate attorney certifies the amendments and re-submits within the legal cure period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies to this financial private-equity SPV; sector oversight rests with the Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) and SEPBLAC for anti-money-laundering surveillance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required — ISIC 6499 (other financial service activities) is not an industrial license category; only an optional municipal activity license (licencia de actividad) is triggered if a physical administrative office is opened in Spain.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) — not triggered for this financial SPV
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical industrial installation, zero manufacturing or processing activity under Law 21/2013 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater discharge or VOC emissions; office-only waste is governed by municipal waste collection under Law 7/2022 on waste and contaminated soils.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: basic fire-prevention compliance under the Código Técnico de la Edificación and a fire-safety certificate (certificado de protección contra incendios) for any leased office premises. Structural load inspections: not applicable for non-industrial office use. Occupational clearance: completion of a risk-prevention assessment under Ley 31/1995, implementation of the company's accident-prevention plan, and registration with the Social Security authority before hiring any staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Spanish Tax Agency; electronic portal: Sede Electrónica (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es) providing access to Form 036 (census registration for CIT, IVA, and NIF), the SII web service, and the VIES validation tool
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign investors must execute a public incorporation deed before a Spanish notary, obtain a provisional NIF from AEAT (Form 036), file the deed at the Registro Mercantil, and then receive the definitive NIF (tax identification number serving simultaneously as the TIN for Corporate Income Tax and as NIF-IVA for VAT). The SL must be registered on the territorial census, designate a tax domicile, and (if non-EU shareholders are present) appoint a Spanish tax representative with sufficient power for tax compliance. Mandatory IVA registration (Form 036/037) is performed in the same census procedure, to be completed before any taxable supply is made in the IVA territory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists under Spanish law; an SL is per se a fully taxable entity for Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at a 25% standard rate. Available statutory elections include: (i) optional tax-consolidation regime for a Spanish fiscal group (Arts. 56–70 LIS) covering 100%-held Spanish subsidiaries; (ii) neutrality/election for reorganizations under Art. 76 LIS (mergers, demergers, asset contributions/segregations); (iii) election of quarterly/semi-annual VAT refund filing (IVA mensual for large taxpayers); and (iv) tax-representative nomination. Hybrid mismatch neutralizing adjustments under ATAD are mandatory, not elective, except where the taxpayer may substantively elect alternative allocation or origination timing; any such election must be disclosed in the annual CIT return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA) / Value Added Tax (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic-turnover de minimis threshold applies to established or non-established businesses performing taxable supplies in the Spanish IVA territory; any person carrying out such supplies must register with AEAT (Form 036) before commencement. For intra-Community distance selling and EU e-commerce sales to final consumers, the Union-wide EUR 10,000 threshold applies: below it, supplies remain taxable in the member state of origin; above it, registration or OSS (One Stop Shop) filing in Spain is required. A PE-buyout SPV that merely holds shares and receives dividends/lending interest has no IVA registration obligation, unless it invoices management, financing, or service fees (services to/from non-established persons may be shifted to the reverse-charge mechanism or subject to the place-of-supply-for-services rules).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing under Law 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece), implemented by Royal Decree 1008/2023, requires issuance, transmission, and receipt of structured e-invoices (Facturae or PEPPOL-compliant formats) for all transactions between Spanish businesses. The SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) imposes near-real-time reporting of issuance and received invoices to AEAT through web services/APIs (XML) within 4 working days of issue (8 for receipts), applicable to taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000 and to those VAT-group registered. The Veri*Factu system (phased in from 2025) will require qualified billing-management systems to generate a secure QR/digital stamp over each invoice record to guarantee integrity and visibility to AEAT; failing to transmit SII/Veri*Factu data is penalized as a formal-tax-infringement with fines up to EUR 2,000 per invoice record.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to third countries and intra-Community dispatches to an IVA-identifiable customer (validated VIES VAT number) are exempt with the right to deduct input VAT (effective 0% rating) under Arts. 21 and 25 LIVA. The exporter must be the exporter of record in the customs territory, evidence physical dispatch/transport outside of Spain or to another member state, and hold the customs export declaration and transport documentation. Services directly related to export (international transport, loading/unloading, customs clearance, international brokerage) are likewise zero-rated under Art. 21 LIVA. For a PE-buyout SPV, zero-rating will generally be claimed only for onward sale of portfolio assets with physical export or for intra-Union services if the recipient is a taxable person in another member state; all conditions must be documented and retained; otherwise the supply is taxed in Spain at the applicable IVA rate (21% standard/10% reduced).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / DUA) accepted and released electronically by the EU customs IT system (Export Exit Release), evidencing the third-country destination and exporter of record
Transport document — Bill of Lading (B/L), CMR waybill, or Air Waybill issued to the Spanish exporter of record, proving physical dispatch and delivery outside the EU or into another member state
Commercial invoice and sales/purchase contract including Incoterms, quantity, price, and buyer's identity/VAT number (VIES validation printout required for intra-Union dispatches)
Inward Remittance Certificate — bank SWIFT MT103 or equivalent credit advice demonstrating payment receipt of the export consideration
Customs valuation evidence and any restricted/linked-good licenses or permits for the specific goods, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may retroactively disallow export zero-rating where the documentary bundle is incomplete or contradictory, assessing the unreported VAT at 21% plus late-payment interest for the ordinary 4-year limitation period (extended to 5 years for large-enterprise taxpayers from 2025) without prejudice to criminal proceedings. Fraudulent or abusive claims attract penalties ranging from 50% (minor infraction) to 150% (deliberate fraud or resistance to inspection) under Arts. 191–194 of Law 58/2003 (LGT), together with loss of deduction rights and prohibition on participating in SII/Veri*Factu schemes. Where the annual defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal tax fraud under Art. 305 of the Código Penal applies, with imprisonment of 1–6 years, fines of up to six times the defrauded amount, and disqualification from tax benefits/public subsidies; retrospective clawback and penalty assessment may include subordinate entities for organized falsification of export documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), together with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business as the competent foreign exchange and foreign investment statistical control authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain has full current and capital account convertibility as a euro-area member state. The euro is freely convertible; no prior exchange-control authorization is required for capital contributions, dividend remittances, trade settlements, or intercompany treasury flows. Profit remittance from an SL is subject to corporate income tax and non-resident dividend withholding tax (generally 19% absent treaty relief) but is not subject to FX approval. The only material frictions are institutional KYC/AML documentation, OECD/EU transparency filings, foreign investment statistical declarations, and Modelo 720 asset reporting thresholds for non-Spanish accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory export proceeds surrender regime. There is no statutory timeline enforced by the central bank, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to repatriate export receivables into Spain. Export proceeds may remain in foreign-currency accounts of a Spanish resident company, provided that balance-of-payments and tax/AML reporting obligations are met. Intra-EU trade and third-country transactions are subject only to standard commercial invoicing and suspicious-transaction reporting rules.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Legally viable only for EU-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions passporting into Spain under Directive 2009/110/EC and Directive (EU) 2015/2366. Practical feasibility for a leveraged buyout SPV is generally Low-to-Medium because most digital EMIs decline complex private-equity holding structures, impose sub-limits, and cannot provide intragroup lending facilities. A digital EMI may be used for operating expenses and minor trade payments, but the core escrow and syndicated-loan treasury should sit with a tier-1 Spanish credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal AML framework permits remote identification under Spain's transposition of EU AML rules using qualified eIDAS certificates or video-identification systems, but in practice tier-1 Spanish banks mandate at least one physical meeting for a non-resident-owned PE buyout SPV. All legal signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, and the compliance-contact director should expect an in-person or video-interview KYC session. Where no director is resident in Spain, a notarized and apostilled power of attorney naming a Spanish resident authorized person is normally accepted, but the underlying UBOs still must be identified before closing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SPV with no operating history and no audited financial statements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and bylaws of ES_SL; NIF/CIF tax identification; notarized board resolution appointing signatories and declaring investment purpose; detailed business plan for the LBO transaction; term sheet or equity commitment letter from the PE fund; parent fund KYC pack including constitutional documents, fund prospectus, regulatory license, and audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-jurisdictional ownership chain involving offshore holding companies and Latin American investors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organizational chart from ultimate natural-person beneficial owners to ES_SL; registry extracts or equivalent certification for each intermediate holding entity; source-of-funds file for the equity commitment; notarized declarations of source of wealth; evidence that all intermediate entities have economic substance and are tax compliant in their respective domiciles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of shareholder loans combined with third-party leverage creating suspicion of opaque debt financing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed intercompany loan agreements with market terms; evidence that shareholder loans are recorded in the statutory accounts; bank statements of the lending entity; ECB/FX statistical declarations where applicable; pipeline transaction documents showing acquisition target, purchase price, and debt-to-equity ratio.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substantial non-EU wire movements from Brazil, Mexico, or other LATAM jurisdictions into the SPV
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth letters from the remitting bank; notarized investor resolutions; chain of title to the injected funds; certificates of good standing of the foreign PE vehicle; evidence that inbound investments are registered with Spain's Register of Foreign Investments; correspondent-bank references for the remitting institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or director appearing on PEP, sanctions, or adverse-media watchlists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent and dated PEP/sanctions screening report from a recognized provider; legal explanation of the screening result if a partial name match arises; official public records or court certificates proving dismissal or non-materiality of adverse media; documented rationale for the commercial legitimacy of the SPV's acquisition mandate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For euro-denominated capital injections from EU investors or the PE fund, the primary clearing rail is SEPA Credit Transfer using IBAN, with purpose code EQUI or INVE and a clear remittance narrative identifying the SPV NIF/CIF, the capital increase or shareholder loan date, and the underlying acquisition deal. For non-euro or extra-EEA transactions, SWIFT MT103 is mandatory, with field 70 referencing the LBO pipeline and field 50K/52D showing the contributing entity. The corporate bank will perform a pre-credit compliance check requiring source-of-funds documentation and the notarial certificate of capital increase or loan agreement. After closing, a post-investment statistical foreign-investment declaration must be filed electronically with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones when the non-resident acquires 10% or more of the SL capital or when the transaction exceeds the applicable reporting threshold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For euro payments to Spanish and EEA suppliers, use SEPA Credit Transfer via TARGET2-Banco de España. For non-EEA, non-euro trade settlements, use SWIFT MT103 with supporting commercial invoice and transport documents. For trade finance against Latin American or other third-country counterparties, issue irrevocable documentary letters of credit via MT700/MT710 or collection instructions via MT400; conditional guarantees and standby LCs use MT760. Any outbound disbursement related to the buyout, including settlement payments, intercompany loans, advisory fees, or the final acquisition consideration, must reference the transaction ID and comply with dual-use export controls, FDI rules of the target jurisdiction, and the bank's payment screening policies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL) with licensed counterparties under ISDA or local master agreements
FX swaps (swap de divisas) for short-term liquidity rotation between EUR and LATAM currencies
Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) for converting fixed-rate debt obligations into EUR liabilities
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted Latin American currencies such as ARS, CLP, COP, and PEN where onshore deliverability is unavailable to the SPV

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the Company's Registered Office (Registro Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than July 30 for calendar-year companies; must be filed within one month after approval of the annual accounts, which must be approved by June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers registry closure (cierre registral), financial penalties from approximately EUR 6 to EUR 60,000, and the company cannot validly file other corporate acts until the accounts are deposited; continued non-deposit for three consecutive years can lead to administrative dissolution and strike-off of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Modelo 200) and Alternative Minimum Tax/Local Surcharge Calculations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria - AEAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days following the six-month period after the tax year end; for a December 31 fiscal year end, filing must occur by July 25.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties: surcharge of 1% plus late interest for each month of delay up to 12 months, and 15% plus late interest for delays exceeding 12 months; tax assessment and collection proceedings, asset freezes, and administrative fines up to EUR 20,000 for formal violations can apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Registry Updating Declaration (Declaración Anual de Actualización de Titulares Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due within one month after any change in ultimate beneficial ownership, and in all cases an annual declaration must be filed together with the annual accounts deposit by July 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalties under the AML framework for failure to keep UBO records and update the registry; registry closure prevents filing of subsequent corporate acts; possible sanctioning of directors and administrative fines up to EUR 60,000 for serious non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is mandatory for an SL if, on two consecutive balance sheet dates, it meets two of three thresholds: total assets above EUR 2.85 million, net annual revenue above EUR 5.7 million, or average workforce above 50 employees; parent companies and certain holding structures are also audited regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Plan General de Contabilidad – PGC) as approved by Royal Decree 1514/2007; IFRS is mandatory for listed entities and permitted for group consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An annual declaration confirming and updating the ultimate beneficial owners must be filed with the Mercantile Registry using the standardized form containing full identity and nationality data of the UBOs; any shareholding transfer or change in control must be reported within one month, and the annual confirmation accompanies the deposit of annual accounts.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created entities...; participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (Art. 21 LIS); ETVE regime for EU/OECD shareholdings; R&D/ICT tax credits; EIC exemption etc.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_regime_note: Indefinite carryforward (no expiry) with annual offset quantitative caps...
